title: Use the second derivative to justify a maximum or minimum
content: Finding a stationary point only tells you the derivative is zero there — it does not by itself tell you whether that's a maximum or a minimum. To justify which one it is, find the second derivative and substitute in the value found for the variable: if d^2y/dx^2 > 0 the stationary point is a minimum; if d^2y/dx^2 < 0 it is a maximum. You must state the sign AND draw the explicit conclusion ('since d^2S/dr^2 > 0, this is a minimum') to earn the mark — stating the value of the second derivative without the conclusion typically does not get full credit. An alternative (not covered by second-derivative test marks) is examining the sign of the first derivative either side of the stationary point.
